title: Goldilocks and the three bears.
lines: Deep in the forest stood a little wooden house.
Three bears lived there.
There was a big daddy bear, with a deep growly voice.
There was a middle-sized mummy bear, with a soft voice.
And there was a little baby bear, with a tiny squeaky voice.
One morning mummy bear made porridge for breakfast.
She spooned the porridge into three bowls.
A big bowl for daddy bear, a middle-sized bowl for mummy bear, and a little bowl for baby bear.
But the porridge was still much too hot.
Come, said daddy bear, let's go for a walk in the forest, and then the porridge will have cooled down.
And the three bears went for a walk.
In the same forest lived a girl with long golden curls.
Her hair was as yellow and as shiny as gold.
That's why she was called Goldilocks.
Goldilocks was out for a walk, and she saw the bears' little house.
What a cute little house, she thought.
She knocked on the door.
Knock, knock.
Nobody answered.
The door was open a crack.
Goldilocks just went inside.
Oh dear, you really shouldn't do that!
In the kitchen she saw the three bowls of porridge.
Mmm, that smells good!
She was so hungry.
She tasted from the big bowl.
Ow, ow!
This porridge is much too hot!
She tasted from the middle-sized bowl.
Yuck!
This porridge is much too cold!
Then she tasted from the little bowl.
Mmm!
This porridge is just right!
And she ate the whole bowl.
Slurp, slurp, all gone!
Then Goldilocks wanted to sit down.
There were three chairs.
She climbed onto the big chair.
Oh, this chair is much too hard!
She sat on the middle-sized chair.
Pff, this chair is much too soft, I'm sinking into it!
Then she sat on the little chair.
Ah, this little chair is just right!
But then she heard crack, crack, CRACK!
The little chair broke into pieces, and Goldilocks fell on the floor.
Plop!
Now Goldilocks was very tired.
She went up the stairs.
There were three beds.
She lay down on the big bed.
Much too high!
She lay down on the middle-sized bed.
Much too soft!
Then she lay down in the little bed.
This little bed is just right, she sighed.
And she fell into a deep sleep.
Snore, snore.
A little later the three bears came home.
Daddy bear looked at his bowl.
Who's been eating my porridge?
he growled in his deep voice.
Who's been eating my porridge?
said mummy bear.
And baby bear squeaked: Who's been eating my porridge, and eaten it all up?
Then they saw the chairs.
Who's been sitting in my chair?
said daddy bear.
And baby bear began to cry: Who's been sitting in my little chair, and broken it to pieces?
The three bears went up the stairs.
Who's been sleeping in my bed?
growled daddy bear.
And baby bear shouted: Look!
Someone's lying in my bed!
And she's still there!
Goldilocks woke up.
She saw three bears standing next to the bed.
She got such a fright!
She jumped out of the little bed, ran down the stairs and out of the door, as fast as she could.
But at home Goldilocks thought about it.
I just walked into their house.
I ate their porridge and broke the little chair.
That wasn't nice of me.
The next day Goldilocks went back to the bears' house.
She brought a basket full of fresh strawberries.
She knocked on the door.
Knock, knock.
And this time she waited politely until someone opened it.
Sorry, said Goldilocks.
I'm very sorry.
I've brought you some strawberries.
Daddy bear glued the little chair back together, mummy bear made new porridge, and baby bear and Goldilocks ate the strawberries together.
And from that day on they were the best of friends.
